newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia borrows funds for gold-mining at 1.5-6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia borrows funds for gold-mining at 1.5-6 pct.

text.p: The Russian government is borrowing 2.8 trillion roubles from 11 Russian commercial banks at between 1.5 to six percent a year to fund gold and precious stones mining in 1997, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
A total of 23 banks took part in the February 19 tender to lend funds, he said.
Banks are willing to accept extremely low interest rates to get into the gold sector in the hope of acquiring more business when the gold market is liberalised, bankers said.
"The funds will be more than enough to make advance payments," the ministry official said.

Russia makes advance payments for gold and precious stones mining at the start of the mining season in spring, to enable mines to start work, and hands over the rest when it buys up mine output at the end of the year, he said.
The banks opened a credit line to Gokhran, the state strategic reserve, which will repay the loan gradually by November, he said.

The finance ministry took into account the interest rate, bank's capital, experience in funding gold mining and the absence of complaints from the Central Bank in choosing the banks, he said. It also took into consideration an appeal from a mining company for financing from a particular bank.
